```{r setup}
#| include: false
# Sourcing DEFINES functions only; the pipeline steps below do the work
# this report and Colab notebook share ONE implementation (no duplicated logic).
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(tidyverse); library(sf); library(lubridate)
  library(ggforce); library(ggspatial); library(maptiles)
  library(quadkeyr); library(prettymapr); library(patchwork)
})
source("1_data_cleaning_spokane_fires.R")  # plotting + helper functions (build_tiles, fetch_fires, plots)

# CROPPED Spokane+Stevens data — built once by 2_geofilter_spokane.R into rds_spokane/.
# report CONSUMES cached artifacts (no re-cropping, no raw CSVs needed).
rds_load <- function(f) {
  p <- file.path("rds_spokane", f)
  if (!file.exists(p)) stop("Missing ", p, " — run 2_geofilter_spokane.R once (from /content) first.")
  readRDS(p)
}
fb_data_bing <- rds_load("fb_data_bing.Rds")
mp_data_bing <- rds_load("mp_data_bing.Rds")
moved        <- rds_load("moved.Rds")
aoi          <- rds_load("aoi.Rds")

tiles_3857 <- build_tiles(fb_data_bing, re_run = TRUE)  # rebuild polygons from the CROPPED tiles
fires      <- fetch_fires()                # WFIGS perimeters (cached snapshot)
evac_zones <- fetch_evac_zones()           # empty layer unless EVAC_ZONES_URL set (maps still render)

# County-line overlay: population_plot()/movement_plot2() read this global and clip it to
# each frame. tryCatch so an offline render just skips the overlay instead of failing;
# tigris_use_cache avoids re-downloading the shapefile on every render. (`aoi` comes from
# 2_geofilter_spokane.R above.)
options(tigris_use_cache = TRUE)
counties <- tryCatch(tigris::counties(state = "WA", cb = TRUE, year = 2022),
                     error = function(e) NULL)

# Earliest/latest windows present in the data (no hardcoded dates) + pretty labels.
w <- compute_windows(fb_data_bing)
first_ds   <- w$first_ds;   first_hour  <- w$first_hour
latest_ds  <- w$latest_ds;  latest_hour <- w$latest_hour
first_label  <- w$first_label
latest_label <- w$latest_label
fires_snapshot_label <- fires_label(fires)

# LEGIBILITY LEVER: frame every map to the fires + 15 km instead of the wide ~224 km
# box, so ~2.4 km tiles are big enough to read. Swap the commented line for the wide view.
# Frame every map to the fires + a margin (auto_fires) so all three fires AND the Spokane
# metro are in view and the ~2.4 km tiles stay readable. Overlays are clipped to this box
# (clip_sf_to_box in the plot fns) so the fire perimeters can't stretch the frame.
report_extent <- study_extent("auto_fires", fires)
# report_extent <- study_extent("movement", fires)  # tighter SE/metro box (crops NW fires)
# report_extent <- SPOKANE_EXTENT
pop_zoom <- 11                             # sharper basemap for the tighter extent

# One shared figure of the two difference/zscore/count windows, framed once.
lon_limits <- report_extent$lon
lat_limits <- report_extent$lat

# --- Evacuation-zone orientation panel (§1a) ---------------------------------
# The z-score map is rendered a SECOND time at a fixed metro extent so it can sit
# beside a screenshot of the county's official evacuation areas (SREC Evacuation
# Address Lookup). This is an ORIENTATION aid, not a spatial join: the screenshot is
# a static image, so any alignment is by eye, anchored on the shared fire perimeters.
# Set EVAC_COMPARE_EXTENT to the lon/lat corners of your screenshot crop. The default
# frames the Spokane metro core and the nearest fire (where the exodus signal is) and
# matches study_extent("movement"); nudge it to match whatever rectangle you crop.
EVAC_COMPARE_EXTENT <- list(lon = c(-117.90, -117.00), lat = c(47.40, 47.90))

# Web-Mercator panel aspect (width : height) of a lon/lat box, so the saved PNG is
# sized to the map's true shape (coord_sf keeps the map's aspect regardless) and the
# two panels crop to the same rectangle.
merc_aspect <- function(ext) {
  R <- 6378137
  x <- ext$lon * pi / 180 * R
  y <- log(tan(pi / 4 + ext$lat * pi / 360)) * R
  abs(diff(range(x))) / abs(diff(range(y)))
}

# Latest MOVEMENT window (08/16 only), labelled for the text. Population and movement
# update independently, so the latest population window (`latest_label`) can lag movement.
mv_latest <- moved |> dplyr::distinct(ds, hour) |>
  dplyr::filter(hour %in% c("0800", "1600")) |> dplyr::arrange(ds, hour) |> dplyr::slice(dplyr::n())
mv_latest_label <- format_time(as.character(mv_latest$ds), mv_latest$hour)

# Shared fill limits across the first+latest windows so a side-by-side pair can use ONE
# scale and ONE combined legend. symmetric=TRUE centers a diverging
# scale on 0. Returns NULL if the column/rows are absent (caller falls back to per-panel).
shared_limits <- function(col, symmetric = FALSE) {
  if (!col %in% names(tiles_3857)) return(NULL)
  v <- tiles_3857 |>
    dplyr::filter((ds == first_ds & hour == first_hour) | (ds == latest_ds & hour == latest_hour),
                  dplyr::between(longitude, lon_limits[1], lon_limits[2]),
                  dplyr::between(latitude,  lat_limits[1], lat_limits[2])) |>
    dplyr::pull(.data[[col]])
  v <- v[is.finite(v)]
  if (!length(v)) return(NULL)
  r <- range(v, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (symmetric) { m <- max(abs(r)); c(-m, m) } else r
}

# --- Network Coverage cross-check (connectivity confound) --------------------
# From network_sitrep_Spokanefires_clean.ipynb (Stage 7): is an emptying tile
# people leaving, or the tower/power dropping? Each declining population tile is
# checked against Meta's daily Network Coverage layer (active / undetected /
# outage-probability). Values are the notebook's headline; keep them in sync with
# the latest run. confounded_share (ALL) = 0.0023; GENUINE_DROP 698 / CONFOUNDED 10
# tile-windows; holds across tau {0.3-0.7} and k {2-5} sweeps; quadkey gate 1363/1363
# exact. VERIFY against the latest notebook run before distribution.
nc_confounded_share <- 0.0023
nc_genuine_tiles    <- 698L
nc_confounded_tiles <- 10L
nc_decline_tiles    <- nc_genuine_tiles + nc_confounded_tiles
nc_confounded_pct   <- scales::percent(nc_confounded_share, accuracy = 0.1)
```



```{r bluf-calc}
# BLUF number computed from data rather than asserted.
.bluf <- tiles_3857 |>
  dplyr::filter(ds == latest_ds, hour == latest_hour,
                dplyr::between(longitude, lon_limits[1], lon_limits[2]),
                dplyr::between(latitude,  lat_limits[1], lat_limits[2]))
.n_exodus <- if ("z_score" %in% names(.bluf)) sum(.bluf$z_score <= -2, na.rm = TRUE) else NA_integer_
```

This report summarizes Meta Data for Good population and movement signals for the days of
available data (Aug 3–12) to help the Incident Management Team (IMT) see **where** anomalous population change is concentrated
and **whether** it is consistent with the active evacuation orders. It is a decision-support
supplement, not a headcount: every figure reflects Facebook users with Location Services on, not
the whole population (see Data caveats).


## Data description

We use Meta's **Facebook Movement During Crisis** and **Facebook Population During Crisis** datasets, which display location activity from Facebook users (with
**Location Services on**) used to estimate how population shifts during a crisis. The data
represent **Facebook app users**, not everyone in the area — henceforth "users." The datasets
compare user behavior geographically near the incident with pre-crisis behavior. There are two
granularities: fixed **8-hour windows** (starting 00:00 / 08:00 / 16:00 Pacific) and **Bing tiles**
(level 14, ~2.4 km or ~1.5 mi squares). For privacy, a window is shown as NA / grey when either the crisis
**or** the baseline count is under 10 users. Grey indicates "one side was below threshold" (not
"no change" or "fewer than 10 people total"). Two signals are used: comparison to a **pre-crisis
baseline** for the same time-of-day / day-of-week (a 90-day baseline for movement and population
datasets) and **raw user counts** are determined at window *T*.

As of this report the latest **population** window is `r latest_label` and the latest **movement**
window is `r mv_latest_label`. Population maps (§1–§2) therefore show the 8-hour window ending
`r latest_label`.

::: {.callout-warning title="Data caveats" appearance="simple"}
- **Sample bias.** this data covers only Facebook users with Location Services turned on.
- **Data intervals.** 8-hour windows, up to ~8 h delay.
- **Tile size.** ~2.4 km or ~1.5 mi, neighborhood-scale, not address-level.
- **Privacy controls.** A window is NA / grey when the crisis or baseline count is <10 (both <10 means the row is dropped).
- **Baselines.** Movement and population data use a 90-day baseline before the crisis.
- **Evacuation vs connectivity.** A tile emptying could mean people left **or** power/cell dropped.
- **Who is under-counted.** The signal skews toward mobile, connected, vehicle-owning residents and may under-capture access-and-functional-needs populations, such as people with mobility limits, no vehicle, or no transit option.
- **Users =/= people =/= vehicles.** Counts are a fraction of residents, and residents may map to more vehicles still (according to AAR, most local households evacuate with two). These figures are not a road-traffic count.
:::

## 1. Per-tile user population: crisis window vs. pre-crisis baseline

The table compares users per tile in the first available crisis window (`r first_label`) to the
pre-crisis baseline for the same time-of-day / day-of-week 90 days earlier. *Most* tiles are near
baseline, but a few show large **differences**.

```{r tbl-stats}
#| output: true
first_day <- fb_data_bing |>
  filter(ds == first_ds, hour == first_hour) |>
  filter(between(latitude, lat_limits[1], lat_limits[2])) |>
  filter(between(longitude, lon_limits[1], lon_limits[2]))

result <- tibble(
  `Number of Users` = c(paste0("Crisis (", first_label, ")"), "Baseline (90-day, same window)"),
  Min     = c(min(first_day$n_crisis,    na.rm = TRUE), min(first_day$n_baseline,    na.rm = TRUE)),
  Average = c(mean(first_day$n_crisis,   na.rm = TRUE), mean(first_day$n_baseline,   na.rm = TRUE)),
  Median  = c(median(first_day$n_crisis, na.rm = TRUE), median(first_day$n_baseline, na.rm = TRUE)),
  Max     = c(max(first_day$n_crisis,    na.rm = TRUE), max(first_day$n_baseline,    na.rm = TRUE))
)
knitr::kable(result, digits = 1)
```

Out of `r length(first_day$n_difference)` tiles, `r sum(first_day$n_difference <= -50, na.rm = TRUE)`
had a difference ≤ −50 (people leaving, ≈ `r round(sum(first_day$n_difference <= -50, na.rm = TRUE)*1.5*1.5, 0)`
sq mi) and `r sum(first_day$n_difference >= 50, na.rm = TRUE)` had ≥ 50 (people entering,
≈ `r round(sum(first_day$n_difference >= 50, na.rm = TRUE)*1.5*1.5, 0)` sq mi).

```{r fig-hist}
#| output: true
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-height: 2.8
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of per-tile user count differences (crisis vs. 90-day baseline), first window."
ggplot(first_day) +
  geom_histogram(aes(x = n_difference), bins = 40) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "Users per tile (crisis − baseline)", y = "Number of tiles",
       title = paste0("Per-tile difference (crisis − baseline) — ", first_label))
```

## 1a. Standardized change (z-score)

The difference maps use data-driven color limits, so one large-influx tile can wash the ±50
signal to pale grey. The z-score is Meta's recommended metric, and it
captures each tile's change in standard deviations vs its own baseline, clipped to ±4 — so
anomalies stand out. Blue = fewer users than normal (exodus); red = more users (influx); grey = no
data. Because it is measured against each tile's *own* pre-fire baseline, the z-score separates
*left because they evacuated* from *empty because it is rural* — which the raw-count map (§2)
cannot — so it is the map we use to orient this report to the official evacuation areas.

### Orienting the maps to the evacuation areas

The two panels below place the latest-window z-score (zoomed to the Spokane metro and the nearest
fire, where the evacuation signal is concentrated) beside a screenshot of the county's official
evacuation areas (Spokane County / SREC *Evacuation Address Lookup*). Both panels show the **same
fires** — the dark-red perimeters on the right and the **Level 3 (Go Now)** areas on the left wrap
the same fire — so a reader can line the two up by the fire shapes and then carry that orientation
to every other map in this report.

Note: the left panel is a static, non-georeferenced screenshot, so the alignment is approximate
and by eye.

```{r fig-zscore-evac-save}
#| include: false
# Render the latest-window z-score at the FIXED evac-compare extent and save it so it can sit
# beside the (static) evacuation-zone screenshot in a 2-up. merc_aspect() sizes the canvas to the
# map's true shape so the panel roughly fills it and both images crop to the same rectangle.
.evac_asp <- merc_aspect(EVAC_COMPARE_EXTENT)
.evac_w   <- 7
.evac_h   <- .evac_w / .evac_asp
invisible(save_pop_map("zscore", latest_ds, latest_hour, "zscore_evac_compare.png",
                       extent = EVAC_COMPARE_EXTENT, zoom = pop_zoom,
                       width = .evac_w, height = .evac_h))
```

::: {layout-ncol=2}
![**Official evacuation areas** — Spokane County / SREC *Evacuation Address Lookup* (BETA), captured Aug 9, 2026 ~00:10 PT. Green = Level 1 (Be Ready), yellow = Level 2 (Be Set), red = Level 3 (Go Now). Per SREC the map is for reference only; check webpage for latest evacuation zones.](evac_zones_srec.png)

![**Population anomaly (z-score), latest data window** — blue = below normal (exodus), red = above (influx), grey = NA; fire perimeters in dark red. Same fires as the left panel.](outputs/zscore_evac_compare.png)
:::

**Interpretation.** Where the compact **blue (exodus)** cluster on the right falls inside a
**red Level 3 (Go Now)** area on the left, the movement signal is consistent with the order. A
fire-adjacent tile that is at or above normal (grey-to-red) *inside* a red zone would instead flag
**possible residents remaining** — worth checking against ground reports, since the city's 2026
wildfire evacuation-drill after-action review (AAR) found a meaningful share of residents do not
leave immediately even after a Go Now alert. *Timing:* the z-score
panel is the 8-hour window ending `r latest_label`; the evacuation screenshot was captured at TODO.

Now the first vs. latest comparison, on the same fixed ±4 scale with one combined legend:

```{r fig-zscore}
#| output: true
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 5.2
#| fig-cap: "Standardized change (z-score, RdBu, clipped ±4); left = first window, right = latest. The ±4 scale is fixed and shared, so the panels are directly comparable. Blue = exodus, red = influx, grey = NA (not 'no change')."
(population_plot_z_score(first_ds, first_hour,
                         lon_limits = lon_limits, lat_limits = lat_limits, zoom = pop_zoom) |
 population_plot_z_score(latest_ds, latest_hour,
                         lon_limits = lon_limits, lat_limits = lat_limits, zoom = pop_zoom)) +
  patchwork::plot_layout(guides = "collect") & ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r zscore-note-calc}
.zt <- tiles_3857 |>
  dplyr::filter(ds == latest_ds, hour == latest_hour,
                dplyr::between(longitude, lon_limits[1], lon_limits[2]),
                dplyr::between(latitude,  lat_limits[1], lat_limits[2]))
.n_strong_exodus <- if ("z_score" %in% names(.zt)) sum(.zt$z_score <= -2, na.rm = TRUE) else NA_integer_
.n_strong_influx <- if ("z_score" %in% names(.zt)) sum(.zt$z_score >=  2, na.rm = TRUE) else NA_integer_
```

## 2. Raw user counts
